message.content:
Below is a concise summary of key tenant‑rights and responsibilities under Texas law (as of 2024). It’s meant to give you a quick reference—if your situation involves disputes, eviction notices, repairs, deposits, or other complex issues, consider consulting a local attorney or contacting the Texas Attorney General’s Office for more tailored guidance. | Area | What You’re Generally Allowed / Required To Do | |------|----------------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may collect up to one month’s rent.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after lease ends unless deductions are justified (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear).
• Written itemized statement required if deductions made. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for habitation (structural integrity, plumbing, heating, etc.).
• Tenants have right to repair-and-deduct if landlord fails to fix major problems after notice. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For nonpayment of rent: 5‑day written notice before court action.
• For lease termination/eviction: 90‑days’ notice for month‑to‑month tenancy; longer periods for fixed‑term leases depending on length.
• Notice must specify reason and amount due. | | **Rent Increases** | • Rent cannot increase during a fixed‑term lease without agreement.
• Month‑to‑month increases require proper notice per lease terms. | | **Privacy Rights** | • Landlord needs reasonable notice (usually at least 24 hours) before entering property except emergencies.
• Entry for inspections, repairs, showing unit, or sale requires prior notice. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, source of income, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or veteran status. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for most residential rentals.
• Certain clauses (like “no pets” or “subletting”) must still respect statutory limits. | | **Subleasing & Assignment** | • Tenant may sublet only with landlord’s consent (unless lease says otherwise); landlord can’t unreasonably deny it. | | **Utilities & Services** | • If utilities aren’t listed in lease, tenants typically pay them directly; landlords responsible for maintaining service infrastructure. | | **Maintenance Responsibilities** | • Minor upkeep (trash removal, lawn care if applicable) often falls to tenant; check lease specifics. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If landlord breaches habitability duties, tenants can pursue damages through small claims court or file complaint with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR). | ### Quick Tips 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully:** Many rights hinge on what’s spelled out in the lease. 2. **Document Everything:** Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of conditions, and maintenance requests. 3. **Know When to Seek Help:** If faced with unlawful entry, retaliation, or harassment, contact the Texas Attorney General’s Consumer Protection Division or seek legal aid services. Feel free to ask follow‑up questions if you’d like deeper detail on any particular point!
